problems.title: Two Sum
problems.description:
Given an array of integers `nums` and an integer `target`, return the indices of the two numbers that add up to `target`.

Each input has exactly one solution, and you may not use the same element twice. Return the indices in any order.
hints: Brute force checks every pair in O(n²). What could you remember as you scan?
For each number x, the partner you need is target - x.
Store each value's index in a hash map; before inserting x, check whether target - x is in it.

problems.title: Contains Duplicate
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums`, return `true` if any value appears at least twice, and `false` if every element is distinct.
hints: Sorting works in O(n log n). Can you do better?
What data structure answers 'have I seen this before?' in O(1)?
Add each number to a set; if it's already there, return true.

problems.title: Valid Anagram
problems.description: Given two strings `s` and `t`, return `true` if `t` is an anagram of `s` — the same letters with the same counts, in any order.
hints: If the lengths differ, can they be anagrams?
Count how many times each character appears in each string.
Use one counter: increment for s, decrement for t, then check all counts are zero.

solutions.python:
def is_anagram(s, t):
    return sorted(s) == sorted(t)

problems.title: Group Anagrams
problems.description: Given an array of strings `strs`, group the anagrams together. Return the groups in any order; the words inside each group can also be in any order.
problems.complexity: O(n · k log k) time with sorted keys, or O(n · k) with count keys
hints: Anagrams share something that stays the same when letters are rearranged.
Sorting the letters of a word gives a canonical key.
Map each sorted key to a list of words in a hash map; return the map's values.

problems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
problems.description: Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return the `k` most frequent elements, in any order. The answer is guaranteed to be unique.
constraints: k is in the range [1, number of unique elements]
problems.complexity: O(n) with bucket sort, O(n log k) with a heap
hints: Start by counting frequencies with a hash map.
Sorting by frequency is O(n log n). A heap of size k gets O(n log k).
Bucket sort: index i of an array holds the numbers that appear exactly i times. Walk buckets from the end.

problems.title: Valid Palindrome
problems.description: A phrase is a palindrome if, after lowercasing and removing all non-alphanumeric characters, it reads the same forward and backward. Given a string `s`, return `true` if it is a palindrome.

examples.input: s = "A man, a plan, a canal: Panama"

hints: Building a cleaned copy works, but costs O(n) extra space.
Put one pointer at each end of the string.
Skip non-alphanumeric characters, compare lowercase characters, move the pointers inward.

input: A man, a plan, a canal: Panama

problems.title: Container With Most Water
problems.description: You are given an array `height` where each value is the height of a vertical line. Pick two lines that, together with the x-axis, form a container holding the most water. Return the maximum amount of water it can store.
hints: Area = width × the shorter of the two heights.
Start with the widest container: one pointer at each end.
Always move the pointer at the shorter line — moving the taller one can never help.

problems.title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock
problems.description: Given an array `prices` where `prices[i]` is a stock's price on day `i`, choose one day to buy and a later day to sell. Return the maximum profit, or `0` if no profit is possible.
hints: For each selling day, what's the best day you could have bought?
Track the minimum price seen so far as you scan left to right.
At each price, update best = max(best, price - min_so_far), then update min_so_far.

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
problems.description: Given a string `s`, return the length of the longest substring that contains no repeated characters.
hints: Think of a window [left, right] that always contains unique characters.
Expand right one character at a time. What do you do when you hit a duplicate?
Keep the last index of each character; on a repeat, jump left past that index.

problems.title: Valid Parentheses
problems.description: Given a string `s` containing only `()[]{}`, return `true` if every opening bracket is closed by the same type of bracket in the correct order.
hints: The most recently opened bracket must be the first one closed.
Last-in, first-out — which data structure is that?
Push opening brackets; on a closing bracket, pop and check it matches. The stack must be empty at the end.

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.description: Given a sorted array of distinct integers `nums` and a `target`, return the index of `target`, or `-1` if it is not present. Your solution must run in O(log n).
constraints: nums is sorted in ascending order
hints: Compare the target to the middle element.
Each comparison lets you discard half of the remaining range.
Keep lo and hi; while lo <= hi, mid = (lo + hi) // 2, then move lo or hi past mid.

problems.title: Merge Intervals
problems.description: Given an array of `intervals` where `intervals[i] = [start, end]`, merge all overlapping intervals and return the result sorted by start.
hints: Overlaps are easy to spot once the intervals are in some order.
Sort by start time.
Walk the sorted list: if an interval starts before the last merged one ends, extend it; otherwise start a new one.

problems.title: Climbing Stairs
problems.description: You are climbing a staircase with `n` steps. Each time you can climb 1 or 2 steps. In how many distinct ways can you reach the top?
hints: How can you arrive at step n? From which steps?
ways(n) = ways(n - 1) + ways(n - 2). Look familiar?
Iterate with two variables instead of recursion to avoid exponential time.

problems.title: House Robber
problems.description: Houses along a street each hold an amount of money `nums[i]`. Adjacent houses have connected alarms, so you cannot rob two neighbours. Return the maximum amount you can rob.
hints: At each house you either rob it or skip it.
best(i) = max(best(i - 1), best(i - 2) + nums[i]).
Keep two running values (prev, curr) and update them in one pass.
